subject.title: Feature Request: Per-model turn limits with auto-revert

question: Should OpenClaw support multi-turn model leases as a core `/model` and config feature, or should cost governance stop at one-turn overrides and external policy?
rationale: This changes public command syntax, config shape, provider/model routing, and persistent session state; source inspection shows the current behavior is intentionally persistent, so automation should not choose the product contract.

options.title: Keep N-turn leases as core design
options.body: Leave this issue open as the canonical product/API decision for `/model --turns N`, warning, auto-revert, and per-model limit config after the one-turn primitive is settled.

options.title: Narrow to one-turn only
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/83565 own the core primitive and close or revise this issue if maintainers decide multi-turn leases are not worth the extra state/config surface.

options.title: Decline core governance
options.body: Do not add core model lease policy and ask operators to manage premium-model cost through config, separate agents, or external scheduling/policy tooling.

recommendation.title: Keep N-turn leases as core design
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open as the canonical product/API decision for `/model --turns N`, warning, auto-revert, and per-model limit config after the one-turn primitive is settled.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session controls and model docs history make this the best available owner for the cross-surface product/API decision.
